description:
A runtime type test for pid, ref or c_pointer is always true, and it cannot be made exact without a representation change, because those values are raw machine words with no tag of their own.

Representation (runtime/src/any_value.rs): heap tags are LIST, MAP, STRUCT, CLOSURE, BITSTRING, PROCBIN, RESOURCE; side-band scalar kinds are INT, FLOAT, ATOM. There is no PID, REF or C_POINTER ValueKind. fz_self returns process.pid as u64; fz_make_ref returns a process-global AtomicU64 counter; a c_pointer is the raw FILE* word. resource is the one opaque kind with a tag (RuntimeTestAxis::Resources), which is why resource(t) rejects wrong values.

Probes (interp and run): a received pid and a received ref both match def f(x :: integer); self() == 1 is true; send(1, :m) with an unproven 1 delivers to process 1. def f(p :: pid), do: :matched called with a received 1.5 prints :matched. A statically known integer is refused at compile time (send(5, 1) violates the @spec), a received one is accepted.

Why the test is always true: Types::runtime_type_predicate (src/compiler2/types/mod.rs) never reads the opaques axis of the Descr (Builtin Pid, Ref, CPointer), so a pid-typed test projects to an empty predicate. RuntimeTestAxis has 11 values and three exhaustive consumers: the interpreter (of_value, matches_runtime_type_predicate), native lower_runtime_type_predicate, and the receive matcher's emit_runtime_type_predicate_region_test (the last two share native_codegen/runtime_test.rs).

lib/ depends on the hole: lib/json.fz type_name has clauses _v :: tuple, _v :: pid, _v :: ref, _v :: resource, catch-all, so today every non-tuple takes the pid clause; the file externs' dtor is typed (c_pointer) -> nil; fz_send(pid, t) is reached from the untyped Kernel.send.

Decision needed before building (not yet made):
1. Tag the kinds: pid, ref and c_pointer get their own ValueKind (or boxing) and a RuntimeTestAxis for opaques. A representation change on all three paths. Makes the tests exact and pid distinct from integer, as in Elixir.
2. Keep raw words: a pid, ref or c_pointer test is an integer test. Closes the send(1.5, :m) raw-word read; x :: pid still admits any integer; json.fz type_name changes behaviour either way.

Fails before, passes after (option 1): fixtures on interp, run and build where a pid-, ref- and c_pointer-typed clause refuses an integer, float, atom, binary and list and admits the genuine value; send(1.5, :m) raises instead of reading a raw word; self() == 1 is false.

Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises unexplained.

comments.text: 2026-11-13, from fz-sc8.149: the runtime kind name used in Protocol.UndefinedError (runtime/src/any_value.rs debug::kind_name) names a pid and a ref 'Integer' because both are integers at run time; Elixir says PID and Reference. When this ticket makes them distinguishable, kind_name gains those two names and fixture 01133 gains the two cases.

title: A pid, ref or c_pointer type test tells those values from every other value
